is whether the non- disclosure/wrong disclosure of the make and registration number of the offending vehicle, in the FIR, is fatal for the case of the petitioner.
Young son of the petitioner has died in the accident, in question.

So far as the contents of the FIR Ex.PW-2/A is concerned, the said FIR, has been registered, at the instance of .
PW-3 Rameej Mohammad.
In this document, PW-3 has mentioned the particulars of the offending vehicle, as 'Truck model -S' number of truck HP and in the last he had read the number as 11.
However, it has specifically been mentioned that of the accident had taken place, due to the rash and negligent driving of the truck driver.
He, appeared in the witness-box, as rt PW-3 and deposed, on oath, that the accident had taken place, due to the vehicle bearing No.HP51-B-5311 bulker, being driven by its driver in a high speed.
This witness, in the FIR, has specifically mentioned that after hitting the scooter, the driver of the vehicle drove the vehicle and fled away from the spot.
38. Similarly, in the statement, on oath, this witness has specifically mentioned that the driver of the offending vehicle, after hitting the scooter, fled away from the spot along with vehicle.

The tone and tenure of the cross-examination also suggests that the happening of the accident, in question, had not seriously been disputed by the respondents, as it has been suggested that the accident, in question, had taken place, due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased, while driving the scooter.

39. The accident, in question, had taken place at 9.45 a.m. and the statement of PW-3 was recorded,
when PW-3 was .
admitted in PHC Swarghat.

40. Taking the judicial notice of the mental condition of the person, who has met with an accident,
in which, the driver of the scooter, had expired and the said person also sustained of injuries, wrong mentioning of PW-3, qua the make of the vehicle is inconsqeutntial.
41. rt
Moreover, at the time of accident, the age of PW-3 was 22 years and at that time, he was a student.

In such situation, when, the driver of the offending vehicle fled away from the spot, along with vehicle, then, the learned Tribunal has fallen into error by giving much importance to the mentioning, by PW-3, about the make of the offending vehicle.
It is not sine qua non for granting the claim that the FIR should have been registered.
42. In this case, in the pleadings, registration of FIR, as well as, the accident, in question, has been denied.
According to the deposition of RW-2, he is facing the trial, arising out of the accident, in question, but, he has turned the said case, as false.

43. The statement, on oath, carries the presumption in it.
Despite the best efforts made by learned counsel for the of respondents, nothing material could be elicited from his cross- examination.
In such situation, the findings of learned trial rt Court under issue No.1, are not sustainable in the eyes of law and consequently, the same are reversed.

44. In view of the findings, given above, the petitioner is held entitled to the compensation, on account of death of her son Gurnam, in an accident with the offending vehicle, being driven by respondent No.2, in a rash and negligent manner.
45. In the claim petition, the age of Gurnam, at the time of his death, has been mentioned as 21 years.
According to the averments of the claim petition, he was serving in IPH department and his monthly income was mentioned, as Rs.7,000/- per month.

46. The petitioner has not produced any document to substantiate those facts, except the oral statement of the petitioner, while appearing in the witness-box, in which, she has deposed that her son was working in IPH Department and was getting Rs.5,000/- per month, as salary.

Age of the deceased has also been mentioned, as 22 years, in the postmortem report .
Ex.PW-1/B and 21 years, as mentioned, in the claim petition.
Thus, this Court is of the view that Gurnam, at the time of his death, was 21-22 years.

47. In the absence of any documentary proof with regard of to the employment of Gurnam, in IPH department, this Court is of the view that his earning was Rs.5000/- per month, at the time of his death.
rt 48.

50. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma & Others versus Transport Corporation and Others (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases, 121, the multiplier of 18 would be just and proper, in this case.

51. Applying the said multiplier, the entitlement of the petitioner for compensation on account of loss of contribution comes to Rs.42,000/-x18 = Rs.7,56,000/-.
52.

In addition to the above, the claimants are held of entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head 'Funeral Expenses', Rs.15,000/-, under the head 'Loss of Estate' and rt Rs.40,000/- on account of parentage consortium.

53. Thus, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.7,56,000/- + Rs.40,000/- + Rs. 15,000/- +
Rs.15,000/- = Rs.8,26,000/-, along with interest @ 7% per annum, from the date of filing of the petition, till the realization of the whole amount, with upto date interest.

54. No other point has been urged and argued.

55. However, keeping in view the facts and circumstances, there shall be no order so as to costs.

47. In the absence of any documentary proof with regard of to the employment of Gurnam, in IPH department, this Court is of the view that his earning was Rs.5000/- per month, at the time of his death.
Keeping in view the above position, as well as, the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court, in National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, 40%, increase is to be given on account of his future prospects.
